abstract: HIV-associated penile anaerobes are associated with reduced epithelial barrier proteins and increased foreskin T cell density, but their relationships with myeloid populations remain unexplored. We analyzed inner foreskin tissues and penile microbiome data from 116 HIV-negative Ugandan men undergoing voluntary medical male circumcision. Quantitative immunofluorescence showed 48.6% of cells expressing the HIV entry receptors, CD4 and CCR5, co-express CD11c. Men with a high abundance of bacteria associated with HIV seroconversion and immune cells (BASIC species) had a greater density of foreskin dermal CD11c+ dendritic cell 2 (DC2) populations. Integration with previously published foreskin cytokine data revealed that the density of foreskin CD207-negative DC2 cells was positively correlated with concentrations of IL-1α, IL-1β, IL-8, CCL4, MMP-9, and resistin. These cross-sectional findings suggest that BASIC species are associated with a broader foreskin immune phenotype marked by increased densities of HIV-susceptible dermal dendritic cells, alongside increased T cells and epithelial disruption.
